patients.summary: Retired math teacher with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, stable angina and giant cell arteritis on long-term prednisone who joins in 2020. From 2023 he accumulates vascular events: recurrent BPH symptoms, ischemic colitis with an incidental AAA, a post-catheterization groin fistula, cholesterol emboli with kidney injury, an adhesive bowel obstruction, mesenteric ischemia after EVAR, and a type A aortic dissection repaired in February 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
68 y/o retired HS math teacher establishing care. Previous PCP retired and the practice closed, he heard about us through a neighbor.

PMH
- HTN, many years, on amlodipine. Home readings 130s/80s.
- Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40.
- CAD with stable angina. Gets a tight feeling in the chest walking up the long hill by the reservoir, goes away when he stops. Pattern unchanged for years. Followed by an outside cardiology group, managed with meds, never stented.
- Giant cell arteritis dx 2019 by outside rheumatology, on prednisone 10 mg daily since. Sees rheum about yearly. No headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication or visual change since.
- BPH dx years ago, got up at night for a while, settled on its own. Not on anything.

PSH: appendectomy around age 45. Lap cholecystectomy before that, he can't remember the year.

Meds: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, prednisone 10 (rheum prescribes).
Allergies: none known.

FH: father MI at 68, also HTN. Mother stroke at 75, high cholesterol. Uncle on mother's side had an AAA.
SH: lives alone in Westfield. Never smoked. A beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week. Retired from teaching algebra and calculus, tutors a little. Walks most days.

ROS: no chest pain at rest, no dyspnea, no claudication, no urinary complaints currently, no GI complaints, no weight change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. No temporal artery tenderness, pulses present. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed scars. No edema, pedal pulses intact.

A/P
1. HTN: at goal on amlodipine 5. Continue.
2. HLD/CAD: atorvastatin 40, aspirin. Lipids today. Angina stable, keeps seeing cardiology.
3. GCA on prednisone 10: per rheum. ESR/CRP today for our baseline.
4. BPH: quiet.
5. Health maintenance: will request old records for colonoscopy and vaccines. Flu shot next month with the nurse.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results released
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Graves, your labs from Tuesday look good. Kidney function, liver tests, blood count and sugar are normal. LDL cholesterol is 82, which is fine on your current atorvastatin. Your inflammation markers (ESR and CRP) are normal, consistent with the GCA being quiet. No changes.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care practice received by fax, 38 pages. Includes office notes 2014-2020, med list, labs, and a colonoscopy report from 2016 (normal colon, no polyps, repeat 10 years). Immunization record lists tetanus booster 2015 and a pneumonia polysaccharide shot in 2017. No shingles vaccine on file.

Scanned to chart, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. Consistent with his history. Colonoscopy 2016 normal. Td 2015. PPSV23 2017. Will offer Shingrix and conjugate pneumococcal vaccine down the line. GCA notes from rheum not in this packet.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given L deltoid. Screening questions negative. Tolerated without issue, waited 15 min. VIS given.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 11/19/2020

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Graves, 68, in follow-up of giant cell arteritis diagnosed in 2019. He has had no headache, scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, visual symptoms or shoulder and hip girdle stiffness. He continues prednisone 10 mg each morning.

Exam: temporal arteries nontender with normal pulsation. No bruits over the subclavian arteries. Normal shoulder and hip range.

Inflammatory markers drawn in your office in September were normal.

Impression: GCA in remission on prednisone 10 mg daily.
Plan: continue prednisone 10 mg daily. I will see him back in a year, sooner if symptoms recur.

Allergies: NKDA
Medications: prednisone 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg.

Rheumatology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing well. Both COVID shots done. Saw rheum in Nov, no changes, letter in chart. Angina same as ever, only on the steep hill. No headaches or vision change. Home BP 128-136/78-84.

O: BP and pulse as charted. Weight up a kilo over the winter. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
HTN - controlled, amlodipine 5.
CAD - stable, aspirin and statin.
GCA - on pred 10 per rheum. ESR/CRP today.
Long-term steroid - discussed checking sugars periodically, A1c was fine in Sept.
RTC 6 mo for wellness visit.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs from yesterday are all normal, including the ESR and CRP. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my old doctor's prescriptions for the atorvastatin and amlodipine have run out of refills. Could you send new ones to the same pharmacy? Thanks, Russ

documents.title: Re: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Done, 90 days with 3 refills on each, sent to your pharmacy.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare AWV, first with us.

Functional: independent, drives, manages own finances and meds, cooks for himself. No falls this year. Hearing ok. Vision: has readers, eye doctor every 2 years.
Cognition: three-word recall and clock draw normal. He pointed out the clock hands were off by a minute.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: none yet; gave him the health care proxy form, he is thinking about naming a close friend from his teaching days.

Interval: no changes. Angina rare. GCA quiet.

Exam: vitals charted. Temporal arteries soft, nontender. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2016 normal, due 2026.
- Hep C screen today.
- Flu next month. COVID booster when eligible.
- Shingrix: recommended, especially on chronic steroid. He'll do it after the flu season.
- Pneumococcal: had PPSV23 2017; conjugate vaccine next year.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, ESR/CRP. RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Wellness labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your labs came back normal: kidneys, liver, blood count, A1c, cholesterol, and the GCA markers. Hepatitis C screening is negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Flu
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Fluzone high-dose given R deltoid, lot logged. No reaction during observation. Pt plans COVID booster at the pharmacy next week.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy notification: Pfizer COVID booster administered 10/25/21. Added to immunization history.

documents.title: Rheumatology letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Rheumatology - office visit 11/30/2021

Re: Russell Graves, DOB 07/04/1952

GCA follow-up. No cranial or polymyalgic symptoms in the past year. No visual change. Tolerating prednisone 10 mg daily without new problems he can name.

Temporal arteries normal to palpation. Radial pulses equal. Shoulder and hip motion full.

September ESR and CRP from your office normal.

Assessment: giant cell arteritis, quiescent.
Plan: same prednisone dose. Return in 12 months.

NKDA. Meds per your list.
